Samir — appreciate the clarity, and thanks for confirming the billing contact. Short answers and next steps below: 

On data residency:
- Provisional position: Redwood can support an EU-residency SLA for production data via the Data Residency Addendum, with the caveat that some operational logs (non-PII telemetry) are replicated for reliability to the US for platform health. If Brightline needs a contractual guarantee of single-region processing for all tokens including telemetry, that’s a higher-risk ask and requires a security escalation (will take longer).

On IP / derivative rights:
- Redwood can accept a limited debugging use right for model outputs (non-attributable aggregation) and a prohibition on using Brightline content as training data. We will propose language that permits transient usage for quality/debugging but excludes persistent incorporation into model training. Laura will circulate proposed clause by EOD 2026-09-11.

Evidence:
- Neha will follow up with the SOC2 artifact share instructions to procure@brightline.com. Expect an access window for the SOC2 link; if they need on-site or encrypted transfer we can discuss.

Billing:
- Karthik, note the counterparty requested net 45. Please confirm internally whether sales accepts net 45 or if we need procurement to move to net 30 for the pilot.

Next actions: 
- Legal (Laura): initial MSA redline + proposed residency/addendum language by 2026-09-11 EOD.
- Security (Neha): SOC2 share instructions to procure@brightline.com by 2026-09-11.
- AE (Karthik/Sean): ask Brightline to return a single PDF of requested exhibit edits (one doc with highlights) to speed review.

I’ll mark this high-priority in the intake queue and will escalate if Brightline proposes single-region telemetry restrictions.

Thanks all — I’ll post the redline bundle to the Drive folder once ready.
